method: Every expectation was written from the sources in src/ by reading them; no analysis tool was run on the sources or on the built inputs, and no tool's detectors or output were looked at. The three inputs are the same program: packed as written, bundled by esbuild, and bundled and minified. main.js and preload.js are CommonJS (require); renderer.js, renderer-preview.js and renderer-settings.js are ES modules. Bundling keeps the file names main.js, preload.js, renderer.js, renderer-preview.js and renderer-settings.js and folds the helper modules (ipc/channels.js, config/defaults.js, config/endpoints.js, lib/markdown.js, lib/settings-file.js) into the entry files that use them. Roles and settings are attributed to the five entry files; that is right for the plain input as well, because the helper modules hold constants, option values, a markdown renderer and a JSON settings file class only: every IPC call, every new BrowserWindow and new WebContentsView, every exposeInMainWorld, every request and every storage access of the five listed kinds is written in an entry file. A window setting is attributed to the file that creates the window or view (main.js), also where its value is written in config/defaults.js. The bundled and minified main.js and preload.js were also run in Node against stand-ins for Electron (outside the repository, not kept); the channels registered and invoked, the exposed members and the channels they touch, and the web preferences of the two windows and the view were exactly the ones listed here (with the editor's sandbox following the stand-in's settings file, see below). Requests and storage of the renderers and the main-to-renderer sends inside handlers and listeners were checked by reading. An expectation states what the program does, also where that is hard to see; what only looks like a finding is listed under absent. webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration and sandbox only, one entry per window or view and key that the code writes; keys the code does not write are not listed with Electron's defaults (the settings window writes preload and sandbox only). The preview pane is a WebContentsView inside the editor window, created with its own webPreferences; its settings are listed like a window's. The editor window's sandbox is `unsafePlugins ? false : true`, where unsafePlugins is read from the user's settings file at run time: it is decided at run time and therefore is not listed; a tool should show that the key is set from a condition and must not report either value as a fact (the default sandbox: true of WEB_DEFAULTS is replaced by it). Storage: the main process keeps its settings in a JSON file through its own class SettingsFile (lib/settings-file.js), not through electron-store or a browser storage; the format has no kind for such a file, so its keys (editor.fontSize, plugins.unsafe, vault.path, recent.files, sync.vaultId) are listed neither as present nor as absent. Requests: renderer.js has a two-function helper `http` whose getJson(url) and postJson(url, body) call fetch with their parameter; each is called once with a literal address, and those requests are listed with that address. The two fetch calls inside the helper are not counted as unreadable, because every request through them has a known address. Likewise the page's preferences go through `prefs.get(name)`/`prefs.set(name, value)`, which use localStorage with the key PREF_PREFIX + name; the keys are listed in full. shell.openExternal and shell.showItemInFolder hand an address or a path to the operating system; the application requests nothing, so such addresses are absent and the calls are not request calls.
